_source: Maui Nui Landscape Conservation Plan (DOFAW, version 2026-09-29), plan .txt lines 1088-1224 (Ch 5d, pp.22-26, Table 3, Figure 3), 3313-3528 (Ch 6j, pp.84-87, Tables 25-27), 5278-6587 (Appendix 2, pp.A2-1 to A2-41: Table 1 persistence and cost, Table 2 strategies and actions, Appendix Table 1 species groups, Figures 5-6 and Appendix Figures 1-3). Group species counts were counted from App 2 Appendix Table 1 on the rendered PDF (pp.A2-19 to A2-27). Persistence values checked against the rendered PDF (Table 26, p.85).

value_definitions.benefit_by_group: Expected probability of persistence (percent) of the species group over 20 years under the strategy: best-guess expert estimate, adjusted for feasibility, computed as counterfactual persistence + (benefit x feasibility) (App 2 Equation 3; App 2 Table 1 and Ch 6j Table 26). It is a persistence level, not the gain over no action. For S1 it is the counterfactual (no action) persistence.
value_definitions.baseline_persistence_pct: Persistence under current management only ('B' baseline in App 2 Table 1; 'C Only Current Actions' in Ch 6j Table 26).
value_definitions.counterfactual_persistence_pct: Persistence with no management action ('C' counterfactual in App 2 Table 1; 'S1 No Actions' in Table 26).
value_definitions.groups_above_threshold: Species groups with persistence of 50 percent or more under the strategy (the MNLCP target; values of exactly 50 are shaded as meeting it in Table 26).
value_definitions.feasibility: Strategy feasibility (average of action implementation probability x success probability). Not reported per strategy in the plan, so null.
value_definitions.n_species: Number of species in the group: count of names in App 2 Appendix Table 1 (pp.A2-19 to A2-27), except Plant Group 1, which uses the plant chapter's n = 42 (plan lines 2255-2279 give n for all six plant groups). Null where the table lists genera or a single group entry instead of species. The plan's total of 374 PTM species cannot be reproduced from the table.

strategies.name: No action (counterfactual)

strategies.name: Existing ungulate fences
strategies.description: Goal: remove ungulates from inside fences to minimize impacts to sensitive species. Maintain existing ungulate fences and remove ungulates within and next to them.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Future ungulate fences
strategies.description: Goal: remove ungulates from inside fences to minimize impacts to sensitive species. Build and maintain two new ungulate fences per year and remove ungulates within and next to them.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Ungulate control outside fences
strategies.description: Goal: minimize impacts to sensitive species from wild ungulates. Hunting programs, landowner partnerships and incentives, corral traps and aerial shooting where fences will not be built within 20 years.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Terrestrial habitat management
strategies.description: Goal: improve habitat for sensitive species. Outplanting and seeding of common native plants, removal of invasive plants, firebreaks, and early response to incipient invasive species.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Stream / wetland habitat management
strategies.description: Goal: improve habitat for sensitive species. Stream barrier modification, invasive species removal in streams, wetlands and anchialine ponds, sediment removal, bioshields, hydrology systems, loʻi partnerships and habitat protection.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Invasive vertebrate predator control
strategies.description: Goal: minimize impacts to sensitive species from predators. Localized trapping of rodents, cats, mongoose and feral dogs outside predator exclusion fences; cattle egret and barn owl control; cat eradication on Kahoʻolawe; rodent-free islets; a predator control response team.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Invasive invertebrate pest control
strategies.description: Goal: minimize impacts to sensitive species from invertebrate pests. Surveys to detect and eradicate or control little fire ants, bighead ants, Argentine ants and western yellowjackets.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Existing predator exclusion fences
strategies.description: Goal: minimize impacts to sensitive species from predators. Maintain existing snail and seabird predator exclusion fences, seabird translocation and social attraction, rare invertebrate translocation, weed removal, and snail soft-release boxes.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).

strategies.name: Future predator exclusion fences
strategies.description: Goal: minimize impacts to sensitive species from predators. New predator exclusion fences for snails, seabirds and waterbirds, cat-proof fences for waterbirds, and translocations into new fences.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).
strategies.notes: App 2 Table 2 S10 lists 20 seabird and 20 waterbird fences; the App 2 Figure 6b cost breakdown lists 20 snail exclosures, 20 seabird and 14 waterbird predator fences.

strategies.name: Landscape-scale rodent suppression
strategies.description: Goal: minimize impacts to sensitive species from rodents. Rodent eradication on Kahoʻolawe and regional aerial rodenticide on Maui, Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi. Does not include cats or mongoose.
strategies.cost_units: cost_total: total cost over the 20-year planning period, millions of US dollars (App 2 Table 1, 'Total Cost (M $)'). cost_annual: cost_total divided by 20, millions of US dollars per year; derived for the explorer, not printed in the plan (the plan gives only approximate annual figures, e.g. ~$45M/yr for S25 and ~$40M/yr for S27).
strategies.notes: Does not include cats or mongoose because aerial rodenticide regulations for them have not been developed for Hawaiʻi (App 2 Discussion).

strategies.name: Existing tools for rare plants & invertebrates
strategies.description: Goal: increase populations of rare plants and invertebrates. Outplanting rare plants, maintaining existing propagation and plant pathology facilities, artificial insect habitat, and arthropod reintroduction.

strategies.name: Future tools for rare plants & invertebrates
strategies.description: Goal: increase populations of rare plants and invertebrates. Cryopreservation, genomics, tissue culture and pollen storage research; new propagation facilities on Maui, Molokaʻi and Lānaʻi; methods to control invasive pests such as naio thrips, slugs, black twig borer and coconut rhinoceros beetle.

strategies.name: Avian disease prevention
strategies.description: Goal: prevent the spread of avian diseases. Maintain and expand forest bird breeding facilities, translocate ʻākohekohe and ʻalauahio to disease-safe habitat, Wolbachia IIT mosquito releases, BTI larvicide, and an avian botulism response network.

strategies.name: Future tools for avian malaria

results_summary.persistence_definition: Probability that a species group has viable, self-sustaining populations over a 20-year period (Ch 5d p.23; App 2 p.A2-6).
results_summary.experts_participating: about 100 land managers and scientists in workshops and focus groups, August 2022 - March 2023; 40 experts provided persistence estimates (App 2 pp.A2-4, A2-6; Ch 3d p.13)
results_summary.selected_rationale: No single strategy reaches 50 percent for every group. S25 and S27 together come closest, are the only combinations that include S3, S5 and S6, and together implement all 17 single strategies (Ch 5d pp.23-24, Table 3; Ch 6j p.84).
results_summary.groups_never_reaching_target_note: Seven groups (all six plant subgroups and freshwater snails) do not reach 50 percent under any strategy after feasibility adjustment (Table 26 caption p.85; Ch 6j p.84).

top_three_single_strategies_count._note: Number of species groups ranking each strategy in their top three (Table 27, 'Groups selecting' row, p.87). Plant Group 4 lists rank 3 twice (S3 and S13).

costs.all_species_average_annual_note: ~$55M per year on average to get all 17 groups to at least 40 percent persistence by considering complementarity across all groups (App 2 pp.A2-10 to A2-11, Figure 5). The App 2 abstract also cites 'average annual cost of $26M' in connection with efficiencies from management collaboration, without saying what it covers; the Discussion gives ~$53M per year to maintain fences and facilities and implement landscape-scale actions (App 2 pp.A2-1, A2-16). Unreconciled; see notes.
costs.upfront_note: Read from App 2 Figure 6b (p.A2-13). Year one carries most non-recurring costs; fence construction continues in years 2-10 and field vehicles are replaced in years 11 and 16.

by_taxonomic_set.note: All four vertebrate groups secured at >50% for ~$40M per year (App 2 p.A2-10, Appendix Figure 1).
All invertebrate groups secured at >40% for ~$40M per year (App 2 p.A2-10, Appendix Figure 2).
S25 is the only strategy that gets any plant group to 40% (App 2 p.A2-10, Appendix Figure 3).

cost_curve_all_groups_40pct._note: Steps read from App 2 Figure 5 (p.A2-12); annual costs are approximate visual readings of the chart, not printed values.

results_summary.uncertainty: Using experts' most pessimistic estimates, all groups can be secured only at a >30% threshold; using the most optimistic, at >60% (App 2 p.A2-14). S7 (predator control outside fences) may harm terrestrial snails where predatory Euglandina snails are present, because rodents prey on Euglandina (App 2 pp.A2-14, A2-16).

actions_list.action: No conservation actions are taken; existing ungulate and predator fences are no longer maintained.

Conduct maintenance checks twice per year and after major storm events on existing ungulate fences that are complete or will be complete by Dec. 2023 (see M2 map). Perform maintenance as needed, including repairing, replacing, or retrofitting/improving fence design, and fence-corridor vegetation removal.
actions_list.target: Existing ungulate fences across Maui Nui
actions_list.timeline: Twice per year and after major storms

actions_list.action: Conduct ungulate control via trapping or aerial shooting within and adjacent to existing fences (see M2 map). Deploy snares and snare warning signs along fencelines to minimize incursions and remove animals that enter fenced areas. Maintain and check traps next to fences with high ungulate activity.
actions_list.target: Areas within and adjacent to existing ungulate fences

actions_list.action: Build and maintain two new ungulate fences per year across Maui Nui (see M3 map) that are not yet funded and not under construction. Conduct maintenance checks twice per year and after major storm events; repair, replace, or retrofit fences as needed and remove fence-corridor vegetation.
actions_list.target: New ungulate fences across Maui Nui
actions_list.timeline: Two new fences per year; checks twice per year and after major storms

actions_list.action: Conduct ungulate control via trapping or aerial shooting within and adjacent to newly built fences (see M3 map). Deploy snares and warning signs along fencelines; maintain and check traps next to fences with high ungulate activity.
actions_list.target: Areas within and adjacent to new ungulate fences

actions_list.action: Conduct education and outreach on management of wild ungulates on private lands.
Work with private landowners to create new ungulate control units to increase hunting opportunities on private lands.

Continue to promote public hunting through hunter training courses, the "Go Hunt Hawaiʻi" website and newsletter, and road access maintenance. Evaluate permits issued, animals removed, population numbers and vital rates using hunter, camera trap and/or drone data, and revise bag limits and seasons as needed.
Issue permits for commercial wildlife removal services.

Create a landowner incentive program that pays private landowners based on the number of animals removed (deer tails) to encourage access, hunting, and removal of axis deer. Funds are capped at 10% of land acreage for lands over 1,500 acres and at 100 animals for lands under 1,500 acres.

Create an ungulate control implementation guide for private and public landowners, including zones for ungulate tolerance (zero-tolerance areas, public hunting areas, other lands) based on carrying capacity and land designation goals.
Deploy and maintain corral traps to remove ungulates outside ungulate fences where fences will not be built within the next 20 years but immediate ungulate control is needed (see M4 map).
actions_list.target: Unfenced areas needing immediate ungulate control
actions_list.timeline: Areas without fences planned within 20 years

actions_list.action: Conduct aerial shooting 6-12 hours per week outside ungulate fences within designated shoot zones where fences will not be built within the next 20 years but immediate ungulate control is needed (see M4 map).

Outplant non-coastal matrix (common) plants and seeds from propagation or the wild across Maui Nui within currently known habitat for sensitive species, and habitat being prepared for them, in areas without predator exclusion fences (see M5 map).
actions_list.target: Known and prepared habitat for sensitive species outside predator exclusion fences

Identify and protect (through planning, zoning or other mechanisms) future waterbird habitat from urban development and climate change impacts.

Build pumping and diking systems for wetlands and drill new wells to extract groundwater, monitor salinity, and maintain hydrological conditions that avoid or minimize disease outbreaks (e.g., botulism) in critical waterbird habitat (see M6 Map 2).
Support restoration and management of loʻi for waterbird habitat, sustainable food and ecosystem services through partnerships with loʻi farmers.
Protect anchialine ponds across Maui Nui (see M6 Map 3) by including them in protected areas or precluding development through zoning or other means, and remove invasive species from them.

Maintain existing predator exclusion fences for seabirds that are complete or will be complete by Dec. 2023 (see M9 map): yearly maintenance and repair, fence-corridor vegetation removal, and traps and bait boxes for rats, mice, mongoose and cats inside the fences.
Translocate seabird chicks into existing seabird fences (see M9 map) and conduct yearly surveys of recruitment.
Use social attraction equipment to encourage adult seabirds to nest inside existing seabird fences (see M9 map), with yearly surveys of recruitment.
Translocate rare invertebrates into existing predator exclusion fences (see M9 map) and conduct yearly surveys of recruitment.
Remove invasive plants inside existing predator exclusion fences (see M9 map) when identified and replace them with common native plants.
Construct and deploy soft-release snail boxes/grow boxes in unpopulated snail exclosures that need regular maintenance.

Build and maintain 4 new predator exclusion fences per year for snails within the next 5 years (20 fences total), each about 1/4-1/2 acre, with yearly maintenance, fence-corridor vegetation removal, and traps and bait boxes for rats, mice, mongoose and cats inside the fences.

Build and maintain two new predator exclusion fences per year for seabirds within the next ten years (20 fences total), each supporting 500 adult nesting seabirds, with yearly maintenance and traps and bait boxes inside.
Build and maintain two new predator exclusion fences per year for waterbirds within the next ten years (20 fences total), with yearly maintenance and traps and bait boxes inside.
Build and maintain new cat-proof (but not rodent-proof) fences for waterbirds in habitats where feral cats are the main predators and/or full predator exclusion fences are hard to build.
Translocate rare invertebrates into newly built predator exclusion fences and conduct yearly surveys of recruitment.
Remove invasive plants inside newly built predator exclusion fences when identified and replace them with common native plants.
Eradicate rodents (rats and mice) on the entire island of Kahoʻolawe (see M11 map).

Suppress rats regionally at landscape scale on Maui, Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi by deploying aerial rodenticide once per year in remote, hard-to-access areas outside predator exclusion fences, away from urban areas, managed for sensitive species, and where localized predator control is under way (see M11 map).
actions_list.target: Remote sensitive species areas on Maui, Lānaʻi and Molokaʻi

Maintain captive invertebrate propagation facilities built on Oʻahu by Dec 31, 2023.
Create and maintain artificial habitat for insects (e.g., bee blocks, pond liners) outside predator exclusion fences in areas that provide habitat for rare insects (see M12 map).
Reintroduce arthropods outside predator exclusion fences in dry forest and coastal habitats up to 2,000 ft.

Expand existing forest bird breeding facilities on land already owned by the state.
Aerially broadcast BTI in streams near forest bird habitat where mosquitoes are breeding (see M14 Map 3).
Create a response network to survey and remove bird carcasses in wetlands and report potential outbreaks of avian botulism.
Administer a one-time preventative vaccine or probiotic to forest birds across their current ranges (see M15 Maps 1-3) to prevent the spread of avian malaria.
